records.title: Democratic voters want Congress to cut funding for Iran war: polls
records.summary: Democratic voters want Congress to quickly cut off funding for the Iran war and are prepared to punish lawmakers who fail to do so, two new polls suggest. With government funding set to expire on December 11, congressional Democrats are weighing whether to withhold their support for any spending bill unless it includes restrictions on funding for the war. Such a move would leave Trump and congressional supporters of the conflict to decide whether to accept those restrictions or risk a government shutdown to keep the war going. The new polling indicates that pursuing this strategy would have considerable support among the Democratic party’s base. Opposition to the Iran war helped fuel Democrats’ sweeping midterm victories earlier this month. Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.) has made the December 11 war funding deadline a key plank of his bid to unseat Sen. Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) as party leader. records.title: Indelible art: the punk tattoo artist preserving an ancient Thai tradition – in pictures
records.summary: When Aod-Sarawut Waewngam learned tattooing at the age of 18, his goal was to tattoo himself. Drawn to punk culture as a teenager, he first saw the art as an act of rebellion. But, as his skill grew, he developed an interest in traditional Thai tattoos. Now he is one of the few to have mastered the ancient art of Lanna leg tattoos, which cover the wearer from the knees to the waist, and is working to preserve the traditional art form while adapting the practice to modern times Photography by Wissarut Weerasopon ‘It opens up doors and minds’: inside Sydney’s tattoo convention Continue reading...

records.title: Secrets by Bob Woodward review – the world’s most famous reporter reveals all
records.summary: The journalist who helped bring down Nixon on false starts, Watergate, and the art of cultivating a source ‘I have always disliked the term ‘investigative reporter’.” So writes Bob Woodward, one of the most celebrated reporters of our time – the man whose Watergate reporting with Carl Bernstein undoubtedly changed the US presidency and journalism itself for ever. His longtime boss, the Washington Post editor Ben Bradlee, disliked the term too: “All reporting is investigative,” Bradlee would say. The term conjures a certain sophistication, perhaps, but part of the beauty of a reporter’s work is how deceptively unsophisticated it can be. Secrets is a far-ranging, revealing memoir of an extraordinary career, but more than that, it is an ode to grinding it out – knocking on doors, asking and asking again, listening, taking notes, making notes on the notes, patiently following every lead to exhaustion. In a media ecosystem saturated with fast and flimsy takes, this feels like a tonic. The real star of his story, Woodward seems to insist, is the shoe leather. Continue reading...

EU Council president Antonio Costa is trying to hasten adoption of the Multiannual Financial Framework, which runs from 2028 through 2034, because next year’s elections in France, Italy and Poland could bring Euroskeptic leaders to power who may want to cut their countries’ contributions. records.title: The Guardian view on the next UN secretary general: sacrificing principles will damn the institution, not save it | Editorial
records.summary: The UK must continue to oppose the UAE’s tainted nominee, Lana Nusseibeh. The ethical course is also the pragmatic one The future of the United Nations has rarely looked more perilous in an age of impunity for atrocities, raging wars, open US hostility, a funding crisis and security council deadlock. It is widely agreed that the choice of its next secretary general is critical – perhaps even existential. Unfortunately, that’s where agreement ends. Under the opaque selection system, security council members are privately polled on their views of each candidate. A “discourage” vote from one of the five permanent members is diplomacy-speak for a veto. Only when a consensus emerges does the general assembly get a say on the candidate. The next straw poll is due on Monday, with no deal yet in sight . With António Guterres completing his term on 31 December, the seat could fall empty for the first time. Caracas said in a macroeconomic framework published on Tuesday that the country's total debt, about 242 percent of GDP, is unsustainable and that Venezuela has been in protracted default since 2017. Venezuela's economy has been battered by years of hyperinflation, sanctions and, most recently, deadly earthquakes. Sadly, these often don’t have the range to cover every room in your home, leaving you high and dry when you’re trying to binge-watch TV or get work done in a distant home office. Wifi extenders and mesh systems can help. Extenders plug in to a mains socket between your location and the router, then pass data backwards and forwards to extend your router’s reach. Mesh systems are even smarter, pairing a secondary router with one or two satellite units, which work together to extend the wifi coverage throughout your home. The mesh system can pass your connection from unit to unit to make sure you’re always getting the best possible link from your device to the internet, wherever you are in your home. records.summary: "Be Ready": Britons Hoard £700 Million In Cash After Crisis Warning Authored by Anastasiia Chabaniuk via Traders Union , UK households are increasing cash holdings after the government urges the public to prepare for potential emergencies under its "Be Ready" campaign.  Bank of England data indicates as much as £700 million has been hoarded over the past five weeks , highlighting how official preparedness messaging is influencing consumer behavior. Cash buildup follows emergency guidance As reported by Bloomberg , citing the Bank of England, the amount of cash in circulation has increased by £1.5 billion since Oct. 22 , when the government stepped up its public readiness message. That increase follows comments from Security Minister Dan Jarvis, who tells people to keep three days' worth of essentials, including bottled water, food, wind-up radios and cash in a mix of coins and notes , to manage through a cyber attack, severe weather or other emergencies. records.summary: Democratic voters want Congress to quickly cut off funding for the Iran war and are prepared to punish lawmakers who fail to do so, two new polls suggest. records.title: The myth of a united Turkic front against Russia, China, and Iran
records.summary: When Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with the leaders of five Central Asian states in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, on October 19, in a format known as 5+1, a sense of contradiction loomed. Just a few days earlier in Athens, Greece, Rubio had spoken against ancient Persia as an invader and destroyer in a speech purportedly extolling Western civilization. Yet here he was, courting partners in Samarkand, a city that epitomizes the historic Persianate realm , whose inhabitants still predominantly speak Tajik , a variant of Persian. The irony was not lost on Iranian diplomats, who took to social media to troll Rubio over the incongruity. methodology.reliability: A official primary source/catalogue; B established newsroom or independent research; C specialist, advocacy or aggregator; D alternative commentary; E unverified social/community; U unclassified. Grade describes source class, not the truth of a specific claim.
methodology.confidence: Claim confidence is left unassessed unless an upstream collector supplies a numeric value. Source grade is not claim confidence.
methodology.corroboration: The six views reuse the existing archive. Similar stories, repeated posts, syndicated copy or multiple outlets quoting one origin are not independent corroboration. A human must inspect provenance.
methodology.geolocation: Location is shown only when supplied by the source or upstream archive. No location is inferred from a headline.
methodology.limits: This is open-source situational awareness, not intelligence agency coverage, an emergency warning service, a live market terminal or a verified threat assessment.
